en: Now,
it's worth noting that we can differentiate
between 2 main types of AI agents.
We have general agents,
like, again, Claude Cowork, that can help
you with a broad variety of tasks because
they have tools that are able to help with a
broad variety of tasks. Tools like reading
files on your computer, but also code
execution tools where the model can actually
write some code. For example, here you see
some code written in the Python programming
language, and then the tool Cloud Cowork can
execute that code to do something, perform
some data analytics here. But you can also
have task-specific agents. For example, in
our company, we built a customer support
agent that runs on some remote server. I'll
get back to that, which we can contact via
Slack. But that's just a decision we made.
Depending on who built that agent, you may
be able to integrate it into other programs
too. And we can talk to that agent about
customer support specific questions because
this agent was built by us to be equipped
with information, knowledge, and tools that
help it with those customer related tasks.
For example, it has tools to look up data on
our course platform. It has tools to issue
refunds. If we wanted to. So it has
task-specific tools. It doesn't need to work
with very broad general tools and write a
little helper program just to fetch some
customer data,
which is what a general agent would have to
do in such a situation.
But instead, it is equipped for this
specific task.
And therefore, naturally, both kinds of
agents make a lot of sense, and in most
businesses and even in personal use cases,
it makes sense to work with both kinds of
agents.
It's just worth noting that naturally,
general agents are the kind of agents that
are built by Anthropic, OpenAI, tools like
Claude Cowork, which you can simply download
and use, versus task-specific agents, which
you
of course have to kind of build yourself
because, well, it's your task and you know
which information and tools the agent needs.
Obviously, Maybe you could think of some
general tasks that maybe apply to more
people, but very often these will be
purpose-built.
In this course, we'll take a look at both
and you will learn how to build
task-specific agents and also more general
agents though.
